questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The mother told the child to __erase__ the extra dots from the given graph.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Create)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"erase"** means to remove or delete something completely, especially by rubbing, wiping, or other similar methods. (मिटाना)

 
 
• **Example: **She used an eraser to erase the pencil marks on the paper.
 
 
 
• **"Create" **means to bring something into existence or to generate something new. It is the antonym of "erase" as creating is the act of making while erasing is the act of removing. (बनाना)
 
 
• **Example: **The artist worked tirelessly to create a masterpiece.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'erase' **is **'create'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Create)**.

• **Delete **(हटाना): To remove or obliterate something, especially written or digital content.

• **Efface** (मिटाना): To erase or remove something from a surface or memory.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

__No sooner had she enter her apartment than__ she found a bouquet of flowers on her table.

options.text: No sooner did she entered her apartment than
No sooner did she enter her apartment than
No sooner has she enter her apartment than

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. No sooner did she enter her apartment than .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the construction **"No sooner...than"**, which is a common way to describe two closely linked actions.
 
• After "No sooner," the correct grammatical structure is **"did + base verb"** in the past tense.
 
• The verb "enter" must be in its base form because it follows the auxiliary verb "did."
 
• The original sentence contains a grammatical error ("enter" instead of "entered" or "did enter").

Correct sentence: *No sooner did she enter her apartment than she found a bouquet of flowers on her table*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Use of "No sooner...than":**

 
 
• This construction emphasizes that one action happens immediately after another.
 
• Example: No sooner did the meeting start than the fire alarm went off.
 
 
 
• **Other similar constructions:**

 
 
• Hardly...when: Example: Hardly had he reached the station when the train left.
 
• Scarcely...when: Example: Scarcely had she sat down when the phone rang.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form.

Shall I meet you soon?

options.text: Shall I have met you soon?
Shall I be meeting you soon?
Will I be meeting you soon?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Shall I be meeting you soon?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is asking about meeting someone in the future, and it needs to be expressed in the **future continuous tense**.
 
• Future continuous tense describes actions that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.
 
• The structure of the future continuous tense is **will/shall + be + present participle (verb + -ing)**.
 
• Option 2, **"Shall I be meeting you soon?"**, correctly follows this structure and expresses the action in future continuous tense.

Correct sentence: *Shall I be meeting you soon?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** will/shall + be + present participle (verb + -ing).
 
• **Example:** I will be working on the project tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will be ongoing at a particular time in the future.
 
 
 
• **Future Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** will/shall + base verb.
 
• **Example:** I will meet you tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will happen in the future but are not continuous.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

The rules of behaviour which guide one in a formal situation

• The word **"Protocol"** refers to the rules of behavior or etiquette that guide individuals in formal situations. (औपचारिक स्थितियों में मार्गदर्शन करने वाले नियम)

 
 
• **Example:** The ambassador followed the protocol while meeting with the head of state.
 
 
 
• **Explanation:** In formal settings, "protocol" ensures that individuals adhere to established rules and display appropriate conduct. (औपचारिक सेटिंग्स में, "प्रोटोकॉल" व्यक्तियों को निर्धारित नियमों का पालन करने और उपयुक्त आचरण प्रदर्शित करने में मदद करता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** It is essential to understand the protocol before attending an international conference.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Protocol**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** She submitted an affidavit to prove her identity in the legal case.
 
 
 
• **Bargain** (सौदा): An agreement between two or more parties as to what each will do for the other.
 
 
• **Example:** We struck a bargain to buy the car at a discounted rate.
 
 
 
• **Impropriety** (अनुचितता): A failure to observe standards or show due honesty or modesty; improper behavior.
 
 
• **Example:** The committee investigated the allegations of impropriety in the organization.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The company __ran about of stock due to__ unexpectedly high demand for the product.

options.text: ran out of stock due to
ran around of stock due to
ran across of stock due to
ran on of stock due to

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. ran out of stock due to .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"ran out of stock"** is the correct expression to indicate that the company exhausted its inventory of products.
 
• The other options such as **"ran around of stock"**, **"ran across of stock"**, and **"ran on of stock"** are incorrect as they do not convey the intended meaning.
 
• The sentence structure is simple and requires the proper phrasal verb that fits the context.

Correct sentence: *The company ran out of stock due to unexpectedly high demand for the product.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phrasal Verb Usage:**

 
 
• **Ran out of:** To use up all of a supply of something, leaving none remaining.
 
• **Example:** The store ran out of bread by noon.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Ran around:** Implies moving around in various directions, not applicable here.
 
• **Ran across:** Means to encounter something by chance, which is unrelated to the context.
 
• **Ran on:** Suggests continuation or reliance on something, which does not fit the scenario.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Clear the decks

options.text: To remove unnecessary things for further work
Prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "Prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Clear the decks"** means to prepare for an event or course of action by dealing with anything that might hinder progress. (काम शुरू करने से पहले अड़चनें दूर करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The team cleared the decks before starting the new project to ensure smooth progress.
 
 

 
• **Explanation of the correct meaning:** This idiom originally comes from nautical terminology, where sailors would clear the ship's deck to prepare for battle or any important activity. It now generally refers to removing obstacles or distractions to focus on the task at hand. (सभी बाधाओं को हटा देना ताकि आसानी से कार्य शुरू हो सके)

 
 
• **Example:** Before launching the new software, the company cleared the decks by resolving all pending technical issues.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To draw something down** (नीचे खींचना): This refers to pulling something downwards, either literally or metaphorically.

 
 
• **Example:** He tried to draw the blinds down to block the sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To take something away** (कुछ हटा देना): This means to remove something from a particular place or situation.
 
 
• **Example:** The waiter took away the empty plates from the table.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To remove unnecessary things for further work** (आगे के काम के लिए अनावश्यक चीजें हटाना): While this is somewhat similar to the correct answer, it lacks the broader sense of preparation implied by "clear the decks".
 
 
• **Example:** She removed unnecessary files from her computer to make space for the new project.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

A student becomes / dearer to the teachers / via participating and actively working / towards the glory of the school.

options.text: towards the glory of the school.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. dearer to the teachers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **dearer to the teachers** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The word **dearer** is a comparative form of "dear" and should be used with a reference point (e.g., "dearer than others"). However, in the given sentence, no comparative context is provided.
 
• The correct expression should be **"dear to the teachers."**

Correct sentence: *A student becomes dear to the teachers via participating and actively working towards the glory of the school*.

__
 
• The blank needs a word to introduce a clause that describes the *place* ("villages") where certain conditions or activities ("agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms") exist.
 
• "**Where**" is a relative adverb used to refer to a place. It correctly connects the location (villages) to the characteristics found within them.

Complete Passage: *Indian villages showcase the country's rich culture and customs. Most Indians live in villages, 1. where__ agriculture, modest living and close-knit communities are the norms.
